frameworks.justification: This framework centers on the dominant theme of assessment instrument development and validation, which underpins most empirical studies in the dataset. It allows for a deep dive into methodological rigor while exploring how instruments are applied across other competency domains.
frameworks.general_objective: To analyze the role of assessment instruments in engineering education, focusing on their development, validation, and application across diverse competency domains.

specific_objectives.text: To examine the methodological processes and psychometric rigor employed in the development and validation of assessment instruments for engineering competencies.
key_themes: Assessment Instrument Development and Validation for Engineering Competencies

specific_objectives.text: To investigate how assessment instruments are used to evaluate transversal and employability skills in engineering education.
key_themes: Assessment Instrument Development and Validation for Engineering Competencies
Transversal and Employability Skills in Engineering Education

specific_objectives.text: To assess the relationship between instrument development practices and the measurement of self-efficacy and identity development in engineering students.
key_themes: Assessment Instrument Development and Validation for Engineering Competencies
Self-Efficacy and Identity Development in Engineering

specific_objectives.text: To explore the application of validated instruments in assessing critical thinking and advanced problem-solving competencies.
key_themes: Assessment Instrument Development and Validation for Engineering Competencies
Critical Thinking and Advanced Problem-Solving Competencies

strengths: Highly aligned with the dominant theme in the dataset.
Allows for a comprehensive analysis of methodological rigor.
Facilitates comparative analysis across competency domains.
limitations: May underrepresent themes with fewer studies (e.g., affective factors).

frameworks.justification: This framework organizes findings by competency domains, reflecting the empirical distribution of studies across themes. It enables a comparative analysis of how different competencies are assessed and their interrelationships.
frameworks.general_objective: To compare and contrast the assessment, development, and validation of various engineering competencies, emphasizing their interrelationships and methodological approaches.

specific_objectives.text: To analyze the assessment instruments and methodologies used for transversal and employability skills in engineering education.
key_themes: Transversal and Employability Skills in Engineering Education

specific_objectives.text: To evaluate the role of self-efficacy and identity development in engineering education, including their measurement and impact on outcomes.
key_themes: Self-Efficacy and Identity Development in Engineering

specific_objectives.text: To examine the assessment of critical thinking and advanced problem-solving competencies, including the development of specialized instruments.
key_themes: Critical Thinking and Advanced Problem-Solving Competencies

specific_objectives.text: To investigate the relationship between motivational and entrepreneurial mindset and employability skills, including their assessment.
key_themes: Motivational and Entrepreneurial Mindset in Engineering
Transversal and Employability Skills in Engineering Education

strengths: Covers the majority of themes and studies.
Enables comparative analysis across competency domains.
Highlights gaps and overlaps in assessment practices.
limitations: May dilute focus on methodological rigor in favor of thematic coverage.

frameworks.justification: This framework links methodological rigor (instrument development) with outcomes (e.g., self-efficacy, employability) and contextual factors (e.g., gender, diversity). It reflects the empirical relationships identified in the dataset.
frameworks.general_objective: To explore how methodological rigor in assessment instrument development influences engineering education outcomes and contextual factors.

specific_objectives.text: To assess the methodological rigor of assessment instruments used to evaluate engineering competencies and their alignment with industry and academic standards.
key_themes: Assessment Instrument Development and Validation for Engineering Competencies

specific_objectives.text: To investigate the relationship between validated assessment instruments and outcomes such as self-efficacy, identity development, and employability.
key_themes: Assessment Instrument Development and Validation for Engineering Competencies
Self-Efficacy and Identity Development in Engineering
Transversal and Employability Skills in Engineering Education

specific_objectives.text: To examine how gender and diversity considerations are integrated into the development and validation of assessment instruments.
key_themes: Gender and Diversity in Engineering Education
Assessment Instrument Development and Validation for Engineering Competencies

specific_objectives.text: To evaluate the role of real-world and workplace learning assessments in complementing academic assessments of engineering competencies.
key_themes: Workplace Competency Assessment through Internships
Real-World and Community-Engaged Learning Assessment

strengths: Links methodology with outcomes and contextual factors.
Highlights the importance of psychometric rigor.
Addresses gaps in underrepresented themes (e.g., gender, diversity).
limitations: May overlook themes with limited methodological focus (e.g., affective factors).

recommendation.reason: This framework provides the most comprehensive coverage of the dataset (~70-80%) while enabling comparative analysis across all major themes. It aligns well with the empirical distribution of studies and allows for a balanced exploration of both methodological and thematic dimensions. The framework also highlights gaps and overlaps in assessment practices, which can guide future research and policy.
